deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 62-64). X is a stratified space whose strata are indexed by an ordered set I; at this stage I is in practice a chain Δ_r.
- X_i is the closed stratum and X_i^* = X_i minus the lower strata is the open stratum.
- For an 'elementary interval' i<j (j the successor of i), V_{ij} (written U_{ij} on p.62) is the germ of a tubular neighbourhood of X_i^* in X_j.
- V_{ij}^* = V_{ij} ∩ X_j^* is the deleted neighbourhood, i.e. the germ of the 'link bundle'.
- These germs are regarded as 'topos-pièces élémentaires' (elementary topos-pieces).

Problem. Determine all canonical morphisms between the pieces. Since they are germs of subspaces of X, the morphisms are inclusions.

Argument on this page.
- Assume the frontier-type condition closure(X_i^*) = X_i for all i, and X_i^* ≠ ∅.
- An inclusion V_{ij}^* ⊂ V_{i'j'}^* forces i ≤ i', by comparing points of adherence, which lie between closure(X_i^*) and X_j.
- If i = i', then 'reasonably' j = j', as before.
- If i < i': since ∅ ≠ V_{ij}^* ⊂ X_j^* and V_{i'j'}^* ⊂ X_{j'}^*, we get X_j^* ∩ X_{j'}^* ≠ ∅. Open strata are disjoint, so j = j'. Hence i ≤ i' < j = j'. Since j is the successor of i, i' = i.

Conclusion. The only non-identity morphisms between the three types of pieces are:
- X_i^* → V_{ij}, the inclusion of the stratum into its tube;
- V_{ij}^* → X_j^*;
- V_{ij}^* → V_{ij}.
By definition no other morphisms between elementary topos-pieces are to be considered.

Next page. This becomes the combinatorial diagram Ĩ, with vertices i^*, [i,j], [i,j]^* and arrows [i,j]^* → [i,j] ← i^*, [i,j]^* → [j]^*. It has card I + 2ν vertices and 3ν arrows, where ν is the number of elementary intervals. The diagram of spaces X_i^*, V_{ij}^*, V_{ij} indexed by Ĩ is the 'diagramme fondamental' (17). The aim is the dévissage of a stratified space (or topos) into a diagram of strata, tubes and link bundles, from which X is to be reconstructed by gluing. For two strata this is the familiar X ≃ X_0^* ∪_{tube} X_1^* with link L: X_0 ← L → X_1^*.
errors: The step 'i=i' implies j=j'' is only asserted 'raisonnablement'. It needs a hypothesis that the germ of X_j along X_i^* determines j, which is plausible but not proved here or on p.62.

Restricting to elementary intervals (j a successor of i) loses information for chains of length ≥ 2. The tube of X_0^* inside the top stratum's closure meets the intermediate stratum X_1^*, so links of deep strata are themselves stratified. A complete dévissage needs all pairs i<j, or flags, as in later stratified-homotopy theory and the Esquisse's sketch. As a model for general stratified spaces, the diagram Ĩ is therefore a simplification or first approximation.
There are minor logical shortcuts: i ≤ i' is derived from adherence considerations only under closure(X_i^*) = X_i.

ideas.what: Decomposing a stratified space into open strata, germs of tubular neighbourhoods and deleted neighbourhoods (link bundles), with only the three inclusion types as structure maps
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / dévissage of stratified spaces via links; holink diagrams; exit-path category (partial version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (control data), Quinn (homotopically stratified sets, holinks, 1988), MacPherson, Lurie / Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (exit paths, 2010s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6 'dévissage des structures stratifiées' (sketch only, no proofs)

ideas.what: Combinatorial argument that inclusions between pieces force equal indices, using disjointness of open strata and the successor relation
ideas.modern_name: Elementary poset bookkeeping for stratifications satisfying the frontier condition

ideas.what: Index diagram Ĩ (vertices i^*, [i,j], [i,j]^*; 3ν arrows) encoding the shape of the gluing data
ideas.modern_name: Shape of a gluing (recollement) diagram, akin to MacPherson–Vilonen zig-zag data / subdivision of the stratifying poset

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up 'topos-pièces élémentaires' — strata, tubes and link germs viewed as topoi — and a canonical diagram shape Ĩ. The project implicit in this setup would be an equivalence between stratified topoi and Ĩ-diagrams of topoi. The notes visibly handle only elementary intervals, and the general case is not carried out.
missed.quote: Par définition, il n'y a pas lieu d'envisager d'autres morphismes entre ces topos-pièces élémentaires.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a topos-theoretic precursor of stratified-homotopy reconstruction theorems (Lurie HA App. A, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine, Barwick–Glasman–Haine). The content is anticipated in spirit by the Esquisse and superseded in detail, so it is mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine bookkeeping step in Grothendieck's stratified-topos dévissage. The overall idea is already announced in the Esquisse, and modern exit-path and link-gluing theory covers and exceeds it. The topos-pieces viewpoint is a nice historical detail but not a new result.
transcription_corrections: The pieces are written V_{ij}, V_{ij}^* on this page (U on the previous page); same objects.
Line 'Comme V_{i,j}^* ⊂ X_j^*' continues with '∅ ≠ V_{i',j'}^* ⊂ X_{j'}^*' written beneath, and 'on doit avoir X_j^* ∩ X_{j'}^* ≠ ∅'.
'(sinon on aurait pas comme on a pas ici!)' is probably '(sinon on aurait ... par ci!)'; illegible, best marked [?].
'morphismes d'ordinaux' is more likely 'morphismes d'inclusion'; the word is uncertain.
Labels before the three morphisms are (*), (**), (***).
Final sentence likely reads: 'Par définition, il n'y a pas lieu d'envisager d'autres morphismes entre ces topos-pièces élémentaires.'
